events.title: CGI specified
events.summary: Rob McCool posted the Common Gateway Interface specification on November 14, 1993 — a standard for web servers to run external programs and return dynamic [HTML].
events.about: CGI turned [HTTP] requests into environment variables and stdin for Perl, C, or shell scripts — the original way to build login forms, search pages, and counters before PHP and app servers. NCSA httpd and Apache adopted it; `#!/usr/bin/perl` in `/cgi-bin/` powered the early commercial web. Every modern WSGI, Rack, and PSGI interface is a descendant of this pattern.

narrative.whyChosen: CGI was the first standard bridge between static web servers and executable backend logic.
narrative.whyImportant: It made dynamic web pages possible before embedded language runtimes and application servers.
narrative.problemSolved: Early websites were static files; developers needed a portable way to generate [HTML] from programs.
